subject: EU in-region purge workflow, proof of deletion, and governance Q&A
messages:
From: Eva Müller <eva.mueller@alphacorp.eu>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@alphacorp.com, sovereign­tylaw@eurolegal.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 08:17:00 +02:00
Subject: Request: EU-only processing + deletion proof for pilot

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our legal/compliance team needs a clear operational explanation of how Redwood will ensure AlphaCorp data is processed only in EU regions during the pilot, and — critically — how deletions are handled across primary, replica and backup surfaces. Specific asks: 

- An outline of the in-region purge workflow (who/what/when), including timelines for primary vs backups.
- Evidence types you can provide to prove deletion (poD), e.g. runbook logs, snapshot hashes, certificate or attestation language the customer can include in their report.
- How SCCs and Schrems II assessments map to your proposed controls (we may need a supplemental doc for our DPA).
- Any limitations (90-day backups, immutable snapshots, etc.) and a proposed governance sign-off process.

Can you provide a short operational Q&A and the artifacts to send to our legal counsel by EOD tomorrow?

Appreciate it,
Eva

Eva Müller
Head of Privacy & Compliance
AlphaCorp EU
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Eva Müller <eva.mueller@alphacorp.eu>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 10:04:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: EU-only processing + deletion proof for pilot

Eva — thanks for the clear list. We're able to move quickly on this. A few quick clarifying Qs to make sure our artifacts match AlphaCorp's internal expectations: 

1) For the pilot, do you require that operator/admin access to the control plane is also EU-resident or is customer-data residency only (data plane)?
2) For backups: are you asking for a hard SLA on backup retention windows (e.g., 30d/90d) or a statement of our default policy plus options we can configure?
3) Are you planning to include the deletion PoD as part of a regulatory filing or internal audit? If regulatory, we should include a notarized attestation flow.

Deliverables we'll produce for you by EOD tomorrow: 
- A one-page EU In-Region Purge Workflow (step-by-step, timelines).
- A sample Proof of Deletion artifact (runbook extract, example audit log lines, snapshot hash sample).
- SCCs / Schrems II mapping memo (high level + items for contractual DPA insertion).
- A short governance checklist for sign-off and requested DocuSign route.

Looping in Lauren and Marcus to pick up runbook and SCCs memo.

— Jordan
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 12:22:00 +02:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Draft artifacts for AlphaCorp (EU purge + PoD)

Team — attaching the initial drops: redwood-deletion-runbook-v1.pdf and sccs-supplemental-answers.xlsx (attachment stubs). Key notes: 

- In-region purge workflow: primary store deletion is immediate (0–5 minutes to mark and delete object), KV cache purge within seconds, replica and cross-region replication disabled for AlphaCorp tenant prior to purge.
- Backups: default snapshot retention for hosted Dedicated customers is 90 days. For AlphaCorp we recommend a configurable 30/90/365 option; full deletion from backups requires a background scrub job that runs weekly and a retention-override ticket to force immediate prune of eligible snapshots. Target P0 timeline for forced prune: 7–14 days after request (dependent on snapshot lifecycle).
- PoD artifact approach: we provide (a) deletion job runbook extract, (b) manifest of object IDs with SHA-256 hashes, (c) a signed audit statement from Redwood ops (notarization optional), (d) logs showing purge job invocation + per-object confirmation.
- SCCs mapping: we include contractual language references (SCCs clause X.Y) and operational controls (in-region processing, access controls, KMS keys bound to EU region). The supplemental spreadsheet correlates each SCC requirement to an operational artefact.

Open questions for legal: whether AlphaCorp requires a third-party attestation (e.g., independent deletion audit) or accepts self-attestation plus immutable runbook/logs. If they want third-party, we need to scope (time/cost).

Attachments (referenced):
- redwood-deletion-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook extract, purge commands, sample logs)
- sccs-supplemental-answers.xlsx (mapping matrix)
- alpha-mtap-purge-checklist.docx (customer-facing checklist)

Action items: Marcus to prepare sample PoD (manifest + signed statement). Lauren to prepare short governance checklist and DocuSign envelope links. Jordan to coordinate with AlphaCorp on operator access question.

— Lauren
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Eva Müller <eva.mueller@alphacorp.eu>
Cc: compliance@alphacorp.com, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 11:05:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: EU-only processing + deletion proof for pilot — artifacts attached

Eva — thanks for the patience. Please find the deliverables attached (stubs):

- redwood-deletion-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook extract showing purge invocation, per-object confirmation messages, and sample log lines).
- sccs-supplemental-answers.xlsx (mapping between SCCs requirements and Redwood controls).
- alpha-mtap-purge-checklist.docx (customer checklist that AlphaCorp ops can follow to request immediate purges).

Summary of the key operational points: 
1) EU-only processing: For the pilot we will configure AlphaCorp’s tenant to use EU-only compute and storage regions (Frankfurt / Paris as agreed). Control plane admin operations are restricted to EU-resident accounts by default for this customer; if AlphaCorp needs control-plane hosting in a different jurisdiction we will flag that as an exception.
2) Deletion workflow: Primary data: immediate delete + KV invalidation (seconds). Replicas: synchronous replication is disabled prior to purge. Backups/snapshots: default retention 90 days; forced prune requires a retention-override ticket and scrub job (target 7–14 days).
3) Proof of Deletion (PoD): We will provide a PoD bundle composed of: runbook excerpt, manifest of deleted object IDs with SHA-256 hashes, audit log extract showing purge job invocation and per-object confirmation, and a signed Redwood operations statement. If you require notarization or independent verification we can provide a scoped third-party attestation (separate SOW).
4) SCCs / Schrems II alignment: Our supplemental memo maps each SCC clause to a combination of contractual language (DPA insertion points) and operational evidence (KMS key locality, in-region ingress/egress controls, access logs). There are two residual items that legal must consider: emergency access by on-call engineers (we can provide jump-host justifications and access approvals logs) and subprocessor access if a subcontractor operates the backup storage — we document subprocessors and offer addendum controls.

Next steps: 
- Please confirm whether AlphaCorp wants the 30d / 90d / 365d backup retention option for the pilot, or to keep the default 90d.
- Confirm whether the PoD will be used for an external regulatory filing (if yes, we will prepare notarized wording).

I’ve included DocuSign links in the checklist for the governance sign-off flow (see related links). If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute handoff with your legal team tomorrow morning.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
